---
title: "Can public records flag NYC buildings at risk of fire?"
subtitle: "Testing which housing and building violations show up before serious fires"
toc: false
---

```{python}
from _pilot import *
from fire_data import blocks as fire_blocks
fire = {r["feature"]: r for r in score(fire_blocks, FIRE_FEATURES)}
c = fire["HPD Class C violations per apartment"]
```

::: {.lead-finding}
In a pilot of `{python} len(fire_blocks)` NYC buildings vacated after fires, their HPD "immediately
hazardous" (Class C) violations per apartment ranked on average at the
**`{python} f"{round(c['mean_pct']*100)}th"` percentile** of comparable buildings on their own block,
using only records from before the fire.
:::

New York publishes millions of housing and building records: every HPD code violation, DOB
complaint, stop-work order and permit. This project asks whether those records, read together,
can identify buildings at higher risk of a serious fire **before** it happens, and which patterns
of owner neglect carry the signal.

## Where things stand

| Stage | Status |
|---|---|
| Pilot: fires (`{python} len(fire_blocks)` cases) | Done. HPD violations are a strong signal; DOB alone is not |
| Pilot: structural collapse (9 cases) | Done. DOB history is the signal; HPD helps only alongside it |
| Case study: 2625 Bedford Ave | Done. City records showed warnings months before the collapse |
| Full study: every fire-damage vacate since 2018 | In progress |
